decisions.executionNote: Approach the left standing bottle with the left hand, gradually leaving the initial configuration; right hand stays clear.
Replan from the interrupted pose with smaller increments, aligning the open left gripper with the standing bottle.
Continue the left bottle approach, lowering toward its body while maintaining the current wrist orientation.
Align the left gripper more centrally around the thermos body, approaching slowly with the jaws open.
Close the left hand around the thermos and make a small test lift; retention will be checked visually.
Lift and carry the visibly retained thermos toward the left dustbin, keeping the gripping command closed.
Carry the thermos over the visible bin opening with a small outward wrist turn, maintaining grasp and elbow continuity.
Release the thermos above the bin and begin a gradual right-hand approach to the standing green bottle.
Withdraw the empty left hand upward from the bin while the right hand approaches the green bottle above the other lying bottles.
Bring the right gripper toward the green bottle body; move the empty left hand to an elevated central receiving posture.
Correct right-hand lateral alignment from the wrist view before closing. Set the left hand to face inward for a later handover.
Close the aligned right gripper on the green bottle and perform a small vertical retention test; left hand waits clear.
The green bottle is not securely retained: reopen and advance the right fingers farther around its body before trying again.
The green bottle has tipped onto its side. Raise and pitch the right wrist for a top-down grasp, keeping clear of the table.
Retry the upward pitching approach with halved increments following the continuity rejection.
Continue the right-hand overhead approach to the lying green bottle, pitching downward while preserving elbow-up continuity.
Align the right hand above the green bottle's body with a near-vertical approach, keeping the left hand stationary and clear.
Use smaller increments after the guard; center and lower the open right fingers toward the lying green bottle.
Lower the right gripper vertically around the lying green bottle, using the head view for lateral alignment.
Close around the green bottle from above and test retention with a short lift before handover.
Green bottle appears retained. Lift it toward the central handover area and gradually restore a more horizontal right wrist.
Present the green bottle upright near the midline with the right hand. Raise the left receiving hand toward a separate higher grasp region without crossing arms.
Align the left open gripper with the bottle's higher body while the right hand holds its lower section near the center.
Advance the left fingertips around the upper green bottle and close while the right hand continues supporting it.
Transfer support to the left hand: open and withdraw the right gripper, then move the closed left hand slightly toward the bin to verify retention.
Carry the transferred green bottle left toward the bin, turning gradually. Withdraw the empty right hand toward its own workspace and pitch for a top grasp.
Move the held green bottle over the bin while the right hand approaches above the pink bottle, keeping arms separated.
Release green over the bin after a small centering motion. Lower and center the right open gripper above the pink bottle body.
Close the right gripper on the pink bottle and make a short test lift. Return the empty left hand toward a central receiving posture.
Lift the retained pink bottle toward the center and gradually orient it upright for handover; bring the left hand to a higher receiving position.
Present pink upright near the midline and align the left receiver with a higher section, maintaining support in the right gripper.
After the continuity stop, use smaller motions to align the left fingertips with pink's upper body while the right hand supports it below.
Seat the left fingers farther around the pink bottle's upper body and close them while the right hand continues supporting the lower body.
Open and withdraw the right hand to transfer pink to the closed left hand, then make a short separating motion to check retention.
Carry the retained pink bottle toward the bin while moving the empty right hand above the remaining white bottle for an overhead grasp.
Continue pink's transport above the bin and bring the right hand to a near-vertical approach over the white bottle, with clear separation.
Release pink over the bin; use the wrist view to shift the right hand toward the white bottle body while lowering the open fingers.
Lower around the white bottle and close for a short retention test. Bring the empty left hand back toward a separated receiving posture.
Lift the white bottle and bring it toward the handover area while turning it upright. Align the left hand in its receiving workspace.
Present the retained white bottle near the center, rotating toward upright, and set the left receiver slightly above the right grasp.
Carefully align the left receiving fingers at the white bottle's upper section, with the right hand still supporting the lower section.
Seat the left fingers around the white bottle's upper section, then close while the right hand maintains support.
Transfer white to the left hand by opening and withdrawing the right gripper, then separate slightly to verify left-hand retention.
Carry the visually retained white bottle toward the bin with the left hand; move the empty right hand back toward its origin with configuration continuity.
Position white over the bin before release and continue the right hand's gradual return toward its starting pose.
Release the final white bottle into the bin after centering it, and carefully complete the right hand's return toward origin.
All bottles have been released over the bin. Return the empty left hand toward origin with gradual continuous motion; settle the right hand at its starting pose.
